Switch between common CVD types and compare against the original.

title: Check WCAG Contrast | Contrast Checker
desc: Check WCAG 2 contrast between text and background. Get AA and AAA results for normal and large type, free in your browser. Copy the ratio, then ship the pair.
name: Contrast Checker
lead: Two colors, one ratio. This runs the WCAG relative-luminance formula in your browser and tells you whether text on this background will hold up.
what: A contrast checker compares the relative luminance of a foreground color and a background color, then reports the ratio against WCAG AA and AAA thresholds.

Designers use it before locking a palette so body copy, labels, and UI chrome stay readable. This version runs the WCAG relative-luminance formula locally, so you can try pairs without sending colors to a server.
how: Set the foreground (text) color and the background color with the pickers or by typing hex.
Read the contrast ratio and the pass or fail state for normal text and large text.
Swap colors if you need the inverse pair, then copy the ratio or CSS color values.
when: Use it when choosing type on cards, buttons, charts, and dense B2B dashboards. Check hover and disabled states too, not only the default fill. Large text (18px regular or 14px bold, in WCAG terms) has a lower bar than body copy.

faqs.q: How does this contrast checker work?
faqs.a: It converts each hex color to sRGB, computes relative luminance with the WCAG 2 formula, then divides the lighter luminance by the darker one (plus 0.05). The result is the contrast ratio shown on the page.

faqs.q: What contrast ratio is WCAG AA and AAA?
faqs.a: For normal text, AA is 4.5:1 and AAA is 7:1. For large text, AA is 3:1 and AAA is 4.5:1. UI graphics and focus indicators often target at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.

faqs.q: Does the tool upload my colors?
faqs.a: No. Color values stay in your browser. There is no account and no backend processing.

faqs.q: How do I copy the result into CSS?
faqs.a: Copy the hex (or other CSS color) from the tool, then paste it into your stylesheet or design tokens. Keep the ratio next to the pair in a spec so engineering does not drift.

faqs.q: Is this a substitute for a full accessibility audit?
faqs.a: No. Contrast is one WCAG requirement. You still need to check focus order, names, states, motion, and real assistive-tech testing on the product.

note: Contrast is calculated in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

faqs.a: Many product UIs land between 1.4 and 1.6 for body sizes around 16px. Headlines often sit closer to 1.1 to 1.25. Measure with your actual font, because x-height changes the feel.

faqs.q: Is letter-spacing the same as kerning?
faqs.a: No. Kerning is pair-specific spacing inside the font. Letter-spacing (tracking) adds or removes space across a whole string. This calculator outputs tracking, not kerning tables.

what: A px to rem converter divides pixel values by a root (or parent) font size so you can paste rem and em units that scale with the user’s settings.
Most browsers default to 16px root, but design systems often set 10px or 62.5% tricks. This tool lets you set that root, paste several pixel values, and read rem and em in one table.

faqs.q: What is the difference between rem and em?
faqs.a: rem is relative to the root element (usually html). em is relative to the parent’s font-size. Nested em values compound; rem does not.

faqs.q: Why is 16px the default root?
faqs.a: User agents typically start at 16px. If your CSS sets html { font-size: 62.5% } or a pixel root, change the root field in this tool to match production.

faqs.q: How do I copy the converted units?
faqs.a: Copy an individual rem or em value, or copy from the table if you pasted a list. Paste into custom properties or utility maps.

what: A spacing scale calculator generates a ladder of spacing values from a base unit so padding, margin, and gap come from one system instead of one-off pixels.
Teams often standardize on 4px or 8px. Linear scales add the base each step. Geometric scales multiply. Either way, you get named steps you can drop into tokens or Tailwind-style spacing maps.
how: Set a base unit (for example 4 or 8) and choose linear or geometric growth.

Copy the values into design tokens or CSS custom properties.
when: Use it when a SaaS UI has 7px here and 11px there. A shared scale speeds reviews and keeps denser Fintech layouts from drifting. Keep a couple of exception values if you must, and document them.

faqs.q: What is an 8-point spacing grid?
faqs.a: It is a convention where most spacing is a multiple of 8 (or 4 on compact screens). It is a starting system, not a law. This tool can generate that ladder from your base unit.

faqs.q: Should I use a linear or geometric scale?
faqs.a: Linear is predictable for UI padding. Geometric jumps faster and can suit large marketing sections. Pick the one that matches how many distinct steps you actually use.

faqs.q: How do I copy the scale into CSS?

Small icons and simple illustrations ship faster as data URIs when you want zero extra network request. Keep an eye on size: large illustrations belong in files, not in CSS.
how: Paste raw SVG markup or drop an .svg file from your machine.
Review the encoded data URI output.
Copy the URI into CSS url(), an img src, or a JSX attribute.
when: Use it for tiny UI icons, empty-state marks, and background flourishes. Prefer files or an SVG sprite when the same asset is reused many times or is heavy.

faqs.q: What is an SVG data URI?
faqs.a: It is the SVG file encoded (often as base64) into a string that starts with data:image/svg+xml. Browsers can paint it without a separate image request.

faqs.q: Is my SVG uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. Encoding runs in your browser with the File API or the pasted markup. Nothing is sent anywhere.

faqs.q: How do I use the output in CSS?
faqs.a: Paste the data URI inside url("...") on background-image, or use it as the src of an img. In JSX, the same string works as a src or CSS variable.

faqs.q: Should I minify the SVG first?
faqs.a: Yes when you can. Fewer path points and no editor metadata means a shorter URI and less CSS weight.

faqs.q: Can I reverse base64 back to SVG?
faqs.a: This page is built for SVG to data URI. To reverse, decode the base64 payload after the comma in the data URI with any local decoder.

note: SVG encoding happens in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

faqs.q: What is a modular type scale?
faqs.a: It is a sequence of font sizes where each step equals the last step multiplied by a constant ratio. The ratio is what keeps the scale musical instead of random.

faqs.q: Which ratio should I pick?
faqs.a: Minor second and major second stay tight for dense product UI. Perfect fourth and golden ratio jump faster, which suits editorial or marketing heroes. Match the ratio to how many heading levels you actually ship.

faqs.q: Does this tool send my sizes to a server?
faqs.a: No. The scale is calculated in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I copy the scale into CSS?
